claims.text: The pseudocode data types are INTEGER, REAL, CHAR, STRING, BOOLEAN, DATE, ARRAY and FILE, and the type chosen must be the one the problem's data actually is.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The type decides what the program can do with the value: arithmetic works on INTEGER and REAL, joining works on CHAR and STRING, and BOOLEAN and DATE hold what testing and ordering need.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A date is held as DATE, not as STRING, because DATE lets values be compared and ordered as dates, whereas a string of characters only looks like one.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A record structure holds a set of data of different data types together as one unit, with each field declared with its own type, so one thing's data is kept as one value.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A record structure is defined in pseudocode with TYPE <name>, each field declared inside with DECLARE and its type, and ENDTYPE closing the definition; a variable of the type is declared like any other, and a field is reached as <record>.<field>.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
